title: Black-winged kite algorithm: a nature-inspired meta-heuristic for solving benchmark functions and engineering problems
abstract: Abstract This paper innovatively proposes the Black Kite Algorithm (BKA), a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory and predatory behavior of the black kite. The BKA integrates the Cauchy mutation strategy and the Leader strategy to enhance the global search capability and the convergence speed of the algorithm. This novel combination achieves a good balance between exploring global solutions and utilizing local information. Against the standard test function sets of CEC-2022 and CEC-2017, as well as other complex functions, BKA attained the best performance in 66.7, 72.4 and 77.8% of the cases, respectively. The effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through detailed convergence analysis and statistical comparisons. Moreover, its application in solving five practical engineering design problems demonstrates its practical potential in addressing constrained challenges in the real world and indicates that it has significant competitive strength in comparison with existing optimization techniques. In summary, the BKA has proven its practical value and advantages in solving a variety of complex optimization problems due to its excellent performance. The source code of BKA is publicly available at https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/161401-black-winged-kite-algorithm-bka .
venue: Artificial Intelligence Review Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: A Collaborative Heuristic and Enhanced Black-winged Kite Algorithm for Solving 3D Bin Packing Problems in Complex Scenarios
abstract: As solving 3D Bin Packing Problems (3D-BPP) involves the consideration of numerous types of items, different sizes and multiple constraints, the existing packing algorithms hardly meet demands for the balance among efficiency, accuracy and robustness in practical applications, such as warehouse management and intelligent manufacturing. In this study, a global-local collaborative optimization architecture that is inspired by the enhanced black-winged kite algorithm (BKA), has been proposed, called col-EBKA, to establish a stable and mappable continuous-discrete transformation mechanism that enables a deep coupling between global exploration of BKA and local optimization processes of heuristic strategies, thereby achieving a balance between search efficiency and accuracy and demonstrating great robustness in solving 3D-BPP. Moreover, a cooperative constraint combining a hyperplane constraint and a region-exclusive placement constraint (Hyperplane-Region Cooperative Constraint) has been defined to reserve exclusive space for special items such as fragile items, fresh food items, etc., thereby mitigating the risk of item damage. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed col-EBKA architecture in solving complex problems, experimental validations have been conducted on the Bischoff and Ratcliff benchmark dataset and a real-world packing case to demonstrate the performance superiority over exiting methods. Results have shown that col-EBKA has achieved an average space utilization rate of 92.69% on weakly heterogeneous datasets and 88.57% on strongly heterogeneous datasets, thereby exhibiting remarkable robustness. In the real-world packing case involving protected-item constraints, the proposed col-EBKA architecture has also excelled in good space utilization under HRCC, offering significant theoretical basis for e-commerce logistics and transportation using robots.
